page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and FMA.

The server provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a lean 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per virtual core. It does not bundle any local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent data. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth capacity of 10 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a significant split between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (1001.0) and stress-ng (1106.89) fall into lower percentiles due to the conservative 2.5 GHz base clock. Conversely, multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate middle-tier efficiency, yielding 23616.79 in stress-ng, 8847.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 18175.0 in Clang software compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.0 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 45.75 GB/sec for writes.

From an architectural standpoint, ecs.ic5.8xlarge delivers cost efficiency for parallelized processing tasks that do not demand substantial per-thread memory. The 1.0 GB per vCPU boundary represents a tradeoff that restricts large in-memory caching or dense virtualization. This instance profile aligns directly with parallel batch workloads, distributed compilation, static web serving (17.02 GB/sec throughput), and compute tasks accelerated by AVX-512 vector pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 32 vCPUs over 16 physical cores and 32.0 GB of memory, it delivers a focused 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance features no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-threaded performance, recording 23,616.79 on stress-ng multi-core and 8,847.0 on Geekbench multi-core, contrasted with lower single-core execution speed. Extended vector instructions like AVX-512 are supported. Given its dense vCPU allocation and compact memory footprint, this instance is suitable for parallel batch jobs, distributed code compilation, and static web serving.
